key_insight: Agentic RSR closes the gap between reconstruction and control by using the same task to drive scene modeling, policy learning, and real-robot execution. The result is a real-to-sim-to-real pipeline that aims to produce simulations that are both visually faithful and robot-useful.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the common disconnect between reconstructing a workspace in simulation and training policies that can actually work on the real robot. Standard pipelines often ignore whether the reconstructed scene preserves task-relevant interactions and whether the policy uses observations available at deployment.
method: Start from a workspace video, a task description, and a known robot model.
Reconstruct the scene with task-relevant geometry and interaction cues so the simulation supports the target manipulation task.
Develop execution-grounded robot policies that rely on observations the real robot can access.
Link simulation and real execution through the same task, enabling iterative real-to-sim-to-real refinement.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this framework offers a more practical path from data collection to deployable robot behavior. It can reduce sim-to-real mismatch and make embodied policies easier to evaluate, debug, and transfer to real systems.
visual_elements: A left-to-right pipeline diagram: real workspace video -> reconstructed simulation -> robot policy -> real robot execution.
A split-view comparison showing task-relevant vs. irrelevant scene reconstruction details.
An icon-based loop illustrating the real-to-sim-to-real feedback cycle.
A small overlay of robot observations vs. simulator observations to highlight execution grounding.
paper_title: Agentic RSR: Real-to-Sim-to-Real through Scene Reconstruction and Execution-Grounded Robot Policies
paper_authors: Yihan Li, Yating Feng, Shengjiu Sun, Jianing Chen, Hao Ren
